concept.subject: A house's gable at golden hour: a steep triangular roof against a clear sky, two red and white striped awnings over white shutters, and tiled eaves along the bottom.
concept.composition: The gable fills the picture: its roof rises from both sides at about seven tenths of the height to a peak at the top center, so the upper corners are clear sky. Two striped awnings, each about a fifth of the picture wide, hang side by side at a little under half the height over white shutters, each casting its shadow onto the wall to its right; a vent sits on the right slope, and tiled eaves run along the bottom, raised in the middle.
concept.layout: 53 round pegs and 94 bricks. The roof's two slopes are long brick slides from beside the cannon to the walls, a row of pegs follows each slope in the sky above it, and a shorter brick line follows the shadow under each slope low inside the gable. A brick band crosses the wall under the peak. The awnings' tops are solid ledges over their red stripes, which stand as short bricks above the scalloped brick valances; the shutters are peg rows, the sills and the three tiled eaves brick rows, and pegs mark the edge of the left awning's shadow and the wall between and below the windows.

difficulty.note: Brick-heavy finale: the slopes carry most balls down the outside of the gable, and the band and the awnings' solid tops keep balls off the stripes and shutters, which are reached only through the gaps beside the band.

background.prompt: A photo of a house's gable at golden hour against a clear blue sky. The roof's two slopes, edged with an olive fascia, rise from the left and right edges at about seven tenths of the height to a peak at the top center, leaving the upper corners as plain sky. On the yellow wall two red and white striped awnings hang side by side, from about 0.23 to 0.45 and from 0.56 to 0.79 of the width, their tops at about 0.46 of the height and their scalloped valances at about 0.62, over white shutters, each casting a dark shadow onto the wall to its right. A small vent sits on the right slope at about 0.78 of the width. Tiled eaves run along the bottom at about nine tenths of the height, raised in the middle; the lower corners show the ends of the eaves and the wall.

picture.title: Close-up of a Spanish house in Madrid with red and white striped awnings under a clear sky.
picture.author: Altamart
